answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that decays over time, like a comet that only shines briefly unless it keeps earning trust. Each agent must lock a small deposit and build a history of useful work; new identities start with almost no weight, so a flood of cheap clones cannot outvote established participants. Think of a sparrow joining a flock: it is watched for a season before its calls carry weight. In a harsh tundra of scarce rewards, sybils starve because each fake identity must pay the same entry cost yet earns nothing without real, verifiable contributions.
